record.one_liner: Neo4j is a graph database queried with Cypher, offered self-managed and as the managed AuraDB cloud service.
record.auth_notes: Two separate surfaces. (1) Aura management API (api.neo4j.io): client ID/secret created in the Aura console, exchanged at /oauth/token (client_credentials, HTTP Basic) for a 1-hour Bearer token. This is a machine-to-machine client-credentials flow, not a third-party-app consent flow. (2) Query API (HTTP, /db/<db>/query/v2) to run Cypher: requires an Authorization header; the fetched page shows only a Basic example (database user/password). Bearer/SSO for the Query API was not confirmed from fetched pages. The official MCP server documents only username/password.
record.access_notes: AuraDB Free exists and is covered by the Aura API rate-limit table (25 req/min for Free and Pro trial without billing). I did not fetch a page explicitly stating Free-tier users can create API credentials, so this is inferred. Self-managed Community Edition is also free and exposes the Query API (enabled by default from 5.25).
record.blocker: No single third-party API: the Aura API only manages instances (and billing); data access goes through the Query API or Bolt against a specific database with that database's own credentials (Basic). No OAuth for end-user delegation. Aura API rate limit is 25 req/min on free/trial, 125 on paid. Full Aura endpoint list was not retrieved.
